title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(元木光雄研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III(Motoki Mitsuo)
educationalGoal: Based on the concrete knowledge of fundamental technologies, students acquire problem-solving skills related to computer & information engineering. Students are also given opportunities to experience R&D activities related to concrete information technology and systems. Through this process, students cultivate advanced abilities in the areas of production process development, information gathering, communications, problem-solving in regional orientation, and making objective evaluations.
advice: Students learn R&D methods in the following typical topics: 1. Proposing and analyzing algorithms 2. Finding new knowledge by analyzing big data 3. Developing a new system by applying some algorithms Students will select a topics from one of these research areas and pursue it as they work to acquire the abilities needed for developing valuable IT systems. Moreover, students will acquire communication skills through academic meetings and conferences. However, since other topics are also acceptable, students are expected to choose their topics through discussions with their faculty advisor.
requiredKnowledge: It is important to accumulate daily results. Students are requested to conduct self-checks at every milestone, such as progress reports for each semester and interim presentations.

activityGoals.body: Be able to set one-year achievement goals in relation to your chosen research.
Be able to set a specific production approach based on your set research concept.
Be able to use your acquired information engineering expertise to advance your design and analysis efforts.
Be able to cope with various problems that occur during the design and analysis process.
Be able to technically describe what you have accomplished in a convincing manner.

achievementLevels.standard: Be able to promote R&D activities smoothly according to the project plan (proposal) that you have created. In the results, it is desirable that students be able to announce concrete results that are based in scientific and technical reality.
